text:
maya: Heads up — dashboards heatmap initial paint is way slower on canary after yesterday's telemetry-proxy change. Seeing ~250ms -> ~1.1s on first tile load :frowning:

samir: which canary? link to the run?

maya: eu-prefetch-3. perf trace: https://perf.redwood/trace/314159 — flame shows long main-thread time waiting on a bunch of small fetches to /telemetry/proxy/tiles

jonathan: that sounds like the change that added per-tile auth sanity checks to the proxy. Did we accidentally disable conditional requests (ETag/304)?

kenji: we added a sync validate step that injects an auth check header. I thought it was noop for cached objects but maybe it breaks caching downstream. digging...

maya: repro snippet (quick):
```bash
curl -v \"https://console.redwood/api/telemetry/proxy/tiles?tile=0x1\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer ...\" -H \"x-telemetry-canary: eu-prefetch-3\"
# response shows full 60KB payload 10x, no 304s, and latency ~80ms/request
```

samir: console build report shows a ~180KB vendor chunk delta too, but the main culprit seems to be the spike in round trips — lots of small tile requests rather than coalesced endpoints

jonathan: did the telemetry client switch from batched fetch to per-tile fetch in the same deploy? I remember a patch around the heatmap lib that changed how we stream tiles for interactivity

kenji: validated in proxy logs: we now add `x-telemetry-validate: 1` on each tile request which bypasses our CDN fallback and disables `cache-control: public, max-age` for safety. that explains missing 304s.

maya: quick mitigation options? can we toggle the validate header off for canary while we patch?

samir: two options: 1) rollback the proxy change in canary (fast) or 2) add ETag passthrough + batch endpoint on platform (longer but correct). I'd lean rollback to restore UX quickly and iterate on batching behind feature flag.

kenji: I can trigger a rollback on the canary. ops side: rollback target eu-prefetch-3 to previous image.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated for service=telemetry-proxy env=eu-prefetch-3 by kenji at 2026-03-20T03:42:12Z

maya: after rollback verified on canary — initial paint back to ~320ms. heatmap lib still +40KB but acceptable. thanks! :relieved:

samir: follow-up items:
- platform: add `ETag` passthrough and avoid disabling CDN caching for read-only tile requests
- runtime: introduce a batched tiles endpoint `/telemetry/proxy/tiles/batch` and have client use it when available
- console: lazy-load heavy heatmap parsing and show skeletons during first paint to avoid jank

jonathan: I'll open a PR for the console lazy-load and add a canary flag so we can A/B the UX tradeoffs.

kenji: I'll open the proxy PR for ETag passthrough + a feature flag to enable strict validate only for write paths. also adding request-level telemetry to measure per-tile RT and bundle impact.

maya: also let's add a quota/routing note: our routing policy currently routes telemetry to platform-proxy for metered customers which multiplies requests across regions — we should route tile reads to nearest CDN/pop when sampling=true.

samir: yes — routing + quota change. We'll coordinate with infra to add a `fast-path` for read-only telemetry in the routing table. I'll create the routing change ticket and attach perf numbers.

maya: one more ask — add a quick dashboard with `avg tile fetch ms` and `304 ratio` so we can detect regressions before UX hits canary users.

kenji: will add both metrics to the telemetry dashboards and wire alerts at +30% baseline.

maya: awesome. thanks everyone. tagging @samir @kenji for PRs. :thumbsup:
